customManagers.description: Track the pinned dotfiles commit that the debug/dev/dev-lite images clone. Without a pin the image content depends on whatever dotfiles HEAD is at build time, so builds aren't reproducible and a bad dotfiles push reaches every image built after it.

Track version pins declared as build args, in any Dockerfile under docker/. Renovate's dockerfile manager only reads FROM lines, so an ARG <NAME>_VERSION is invisible to it and would never move. Each pin declares its own datasource in a preceding '# renovate:' comment.

packageRules.description: Supply-chain cooldown: a release is only proposed once it has been public for 3 days, which is usually long enough for a compromised or broken release of an action, a build-arg pin or a mise tool to be caught and pulled upstream before it reaches CI or an image. Security fixes bypass it. Updates whose datasource gives no release timestamp are held (listed under Pending Status Checks on the Dependency Dashboard, where they can be approved) unless a rule below exempts them.
The same cooldown for every container image: base images, docker:// actions and the image-backed build-arg pins.

Registries other than Docker Hub return no release timestamp, so the cooldown above would hold their updates forever - ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the base of the runner images, among them. They are raised without the age check instead.
GitHub-hosted runner labels (runs-on) carry no release timestamp, and there is no third-party release to wait out.

Everything the customManagers and the mise manager pick up out of an active image's directory lands as 'build', matching how base image bumps are committed, so release-please cuts a patch release for the affected image. Listed before the more specific rules below so they can refine it.

Base image bumps for released images land as 'build' so release-please cuts a patch release for the affected image. Digests are pinned (index/manifest-list digest, so multi-arch builds still resolve per-platform) - upstream rebuilds a floating tag like debian:13 without changing the tag string, and only a digest bump catches that.

Templates aren't built/released by this pipeline (no release-please package exists for docker/templates/**) - keep them updated without implying a release is needed. Digests are pinned for the same reason as docker/utils/**: a floating tag can move without the tag string changing, and only a digest bump catches that.

Every image cloning dotfiles moves together in a single PR - the pin exists to make builds reproducible, not to let images drift apart from one another. 'build' so each affected image still gets its patch release. Run shell/bump-dotfiles-ref.sh to do the same bump by hand. No cooldown: it is this owner's own repository, and git-refs has no release timestamp, so the cooldown would hold it forever.
Deprecated legacy images are not released anymore, skip churn.
